analysis:
Both changed files are documentation only: docs/operations/provider-release.md (head lines 484-1052, plus a version-note rewrite and a date bump in the patch excerpt) and docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md (patch at base ~676 and base text 1-471). No executable code, workflow, script or permission change is supplied, so nothing here weakens a threat-model control.

provider-release.md: the described release chain stays consistent with the threat model. The signing job has no R2 credentials. Staging and publication are separate jobs. The dev-branch lane relies on a ruleset (review, signed commits, bypass list), and that ruleset is not visible in the supplied evidence. The text says `secrets: inherit` is read only behind environment guards, pinned by scripts/test-release-dev-branch.py. I did not see that test or the workflow, so the claim is unverified from this evidence. Registration is described as not authorizing serving, and runtime Apple verification plus matching official hashes remain required, which is consistent with TB-011/T-052/T-054. The doc notes the coordinator trusts source/run provenance from the authenticated pipeline. The cluster_runtime block derives approvals, grants and qualifications from the release payload. This is platform-owned and enabled per environment by variable, and the doc says it is not to be sent to a coordinator that lacks support. Its correctness is outside this repo's evidence.

two-mac-cluster.md: the patch changes the stop-while-starting semantics. A counted stop from the leading Mac's status replaces a 20-second stopped-status heuristic. This is a UX and availability description. Whether the code authenticates stop counts, and whether a follower can be spoofed over the cable, is not visible here. I raise no finding, but the underlying implementation change in ClusterOnboardingDriver/ControlReply is not part of the supplied evidence and may merit review in a code batch.

No concrete security regression is identified from these documentation changes.
